name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Do it: Auto-apply whitespace-only patches to third-party dependencies using Pret. It’s safe, reversible, and fixes formatting drift without touching logic—no risk of breaking behavior. The trade-off is dependency on Pret’s parser, but it’s a lightweight tool with no runtime impact.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just upstream noise—it’s that auto-applying whitespace patches to third-party code introduces silent divergence from upstream, making future updates harder to merge. A safer alternative is to enforce formatting standards in your own codebase via CI checks, not runtime patches. Settle it by proving the cost of manual formatting fixes in your repo outweighs the risk of dependency drift.
